title: Liquid AI Releases LiquidCodec: 74M Audio Codec Explained
summary: Liquid AI launched LiquidCodec, a 74M-parameter streaming audio codec encoding 361x faster than real time. Powers LFM3-Audio-2B and LFM3-Omni-2B models.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Liquid AI officially launched LiquidCodec on November 12, 2026, a 74-million parameter streaming audio codec.
- The codec encodes audio 361 times faster than real time on a single CPU thread.
- LiquidCodec powers the LFM3-Audio-2B and LFM3-Omni-2B foundation models with 12.5 Hz processing.


Liquid AI officially released LiquidCodec on November 12, 2026, a compact streaming audio codec designed to power next-generation audio and multimodal foundation models. With approximately 74 million parameters, the codec delivers real-time audio compression at unprecedented speeds, encoding 361 times faster than real time on a single CPU thread. LiquidCodec serves as the audio backbone for Liquid AI's LFM3-Audio-2B and LFM3-Omni-2B models, enabling efficient audio processing in resource-constrained environments.


## Architecture and Performance


LiquidCodec operates at 12.5 Hz with a 12-codebook structure, compressing raw audio into discrete tokens suitable for transformer-based language models. The codec achieves its speed advantage through parameter-efficient design, balancing compression quality with computational overhead. Running on a single CPU thread, the system can process approximately six minutes of audio per second of wall-clock time, making it viable for deployment on edge devices and mobile platforms.


The 74-million parameter count positions LiquidCodec as one of the most compact neural audio codecs in production. Traditional audio codecs like Opus and AAC rely on handcrafted signal processing, while recent neural approaches such as EnCodec and SoundStream typically exceed 100 million parameters. Liquid AI's architecture demonstrates that effective audio compression does not require massive parameter budgets, opening new possibilities for on-device audio intelligence.


## Integration with Foundation Models


LiquidCodec was engineered specifically to support Liquid AI's audio and multimodal foundation models. The LFM3-Audio-2B model processes audio tokens generated by LiquidCodec, enabling tasks like speech recognition, audio generation, and acoustic scene understanding. The LFM3-Omni-2B variant extends this capability to multimodal inputs, combining audio tokens with vision and text representations.


- 12.5 Hz processing rate aligns with typical speech prosody patterns
- 12 codebooks provide hierarchical audio feature extraction
- Discrete tokenization enables seamless integration with language model architectures
- Single-thread CPU inference removes GPU dependency for encoding


## Release Date and Availability


Officially released on November 12, 2026, LiquidCodec is now available through Liquid AI's developer platform. The company has not disclosed full licensing terms, but the codec appears positioned for commercial deployment in enterprise audio applications. Liquid AI emphasized the codec's production readiness, citing extensive internal testing across diverse audio conditions including noisy environments, multiple languages, and music content.


## Technical Differentiation


What sets LiquidCodec apart from competing neural codecs is its focus on streaming efficiency rather than pure reconstruction quality. While codecs like Meta's EnCodec prioritize high-fidelity audio reproduction at lower bitrates, LiquidCodec optimizes for low-latency streaming scenarios where real-time processing matters more than perceptual transparency. The 12-codebook design allows progressive refinement, where early codebooks capture coarse structure and later codebooks add detail.


The codec's CPU-friendly architecture suggests Liquid AI anticipates deployment in bandwidth-constrained or compute-limited settings. By avoiding GPU acceleration requirements, LiquidCodec can run on IoT devices, mobile phones, and edge servers without specialized hardware. This architectural choice reflects broader industry trends toward efficient AI models that democratize access to advanced capabilities.


## What This Means


LiquidCodec represents a strategic move by Liquid AI to control the full audio processing stack for its foundation models. By developing a custom codec rather than relying on third-party compression algorithms, the company gains flexibility in model architecture, training efficiency, and deployment footprint. The 361x real-time encoding speed enables applications previously bottlenecked by audio preprocessing, from live transcription to real-time audio synthesis. As multimodal AI systems increasingly incorporate audio alongside vision and text, compact and fast codecs like LiquidCodec become critical infrastructure components.
